[[File:Small icosacronic hexecontahedron.stl|thumb|3D model of a small icosacronic hexecontahedron]]
In [[geometry]], the '''small icosacronic hexecontahedron''' (or '''small lanceal trisicosahedron''') is a nonconvex [[Isohedral figure|isohedral]] [[polyhedron]]. It is the [[Dual polyhedron|dual]] of the [[uniform star polyhedron|uniform]] [[small icosicosidodecahedron]]. Its faces are [[Kite (geometry)|kites]]. Part of each kite lies inside the solid, hence is invisible in solid models.

== Proportions==

The kites have two angles of <math>\arccos(\frac{3}{4}-\frac{1}{20}\sqrt{5})\approx 50.342\,524\,343\,87^{\circ}</math>, one of <math>\arccos(-\frac{1}{12}-\frac{19}{60}\sqrt{5})\approx 142.318\,554\,460\,55^{\circ}</math> and one of <math>\arccos(-\frac{5}{12}-\frac{1}{60}\sqrt{5})\approx 116.996\,396\,851\,70^{\circ}</math>. The [[dihedral angle]] equals <math>\arccos(\frac{-44-3\sqrt{5}}{61})\approx 146.230\,659\,755\,53^{\circ}</math>. The ratio between the lengths of the long and short edges is <math>\frac{31+5\sqrt{5}}{38}\approx 1.110\,008\,944\,41</math>.
